thread:
alex.g: Seeing a pretty clear p95/p99 regression after the runtime rollout last night — users are reporting timeouts and higher tail latency. Not sure if canary missed anything.
maya: I saw the alert too. Which deploy are you referring to? full rollout or canary?
alex.g: Full rollout of runtime v3.1.2 at 2026-03-14T23:10Z. Canary was 10% for ~30m, then we ramped. Metrics: p95 jumped from ~120ms -> ~430ms, p99 from ~320ms -> ~1.2s for text-generation API in us-west.
jon_sre: Confirming graph in datadog, spike starts ~23:12 UTC and correlates with deploy.
lina_obs: Query I ran (Datadog): `avg(last_5m):percentile(aws.request.duration_ms{env:prod,service=runtime,region:us-west},95)` shows the same. Also traces show longer queuing time in the runtime worker pods.
kai_rt: Deploy-bot shows rollout steps. @deploy-bot can you paste the rollout manifest/changes?
deploy-bot: Deployed runtime v3.1.2 -> image: redwood/runtime:3.1.2
Changeset: 
  - enable dynamic-batch-window (default 8ms -> 12ms)
  - bump kv-cache max-entries 20%
  - updated attention-kernel selector for A100
maya: Dynamic batch window change stands out. If batch window is longer we could be holding requests waiting for batch fill which increases tail. But that usually helps throughput, not p99.
jon_sre: Tracing suggests queue_time increased not service_time. Example trace: `trace_id=abcd1234, queue_ms=950, service_ms=120`. So requests are waiting in front of worker. That points to scheduling / threadpool / batching change.
alex.g: Can we reproduce on canary? Canary nodes still running v3.1.2? Or were they replaced with rollback?
kai_rt: Canary was promoted as part of rollout. I still have a canary set with 10% traffic for one AZ. Running a quick load test now.
lina_obs: Also noticed increased GC pauses in the new image on pods: `jvm.pause_ms` spikes aligned with queue time. Maybe kernel change triggered more allocs per request.
sam_product: Customers on chat saw slow interactive responses around 23:30, some timed out at 2s. We have a couple of high-visibility tickets. Need an ETA on mitigation.
maya: Short plan: 1) rollback to v3.1.1 in us-west only (partial rollback) to verify absence of regression, 2) if rollback fixes tail, keep rollback while we bisect changeset, 3) if rollback doesn't fix, failover traffic to other region or scale up.
jon_sre: Agreed. I'll trigger a targeted rollback in us-west for the runtime service and monitor p95/p99.
deploy-bot: Rolling back runtime to redwood/runtime:3.1.1 in cluster: prod-us-west-1 (canary remains unchanged)
lina_obs: After rollback start: p95 down to ~140ms within 6 minutes. p99 trending toward 360ms. Looks like rollback improved tail.
alex.g: Good. That suggests the change in 3.1.2 is causal. We should do a bisect across the three changes in the changelog.
kai_rt: I'll run a sequence of canary builds toggling each change: 1) dynamic-batch-window revert, 2) kv-cache revert, 3) attention-kernel selector revert. We'll test each on a canary with load and check queue times.
maya: Start with dynamic-batch-window revert since traces pointed to queue_time increase. Also add a metric for batch_size distribution: `runtime.batch.size{service:runtime}` — we need to see if larger batches are forming.
jon_sre: Running a synthetic at 200rps to the canary with dynamic-window reverted now. Early look: queue_time stable, p99 sub-300ms.
lina_obs: When we flip dynamic-window back we see average batch_size drop from 6.1 -> 3.8 and queue_time falls.
kai_rt: Ok confirmed locally: dynamic-window increase caused the runtime to hold requests longer to try and form larger batches. That improved throughput but hurt tails during bursty traffic — exactly our customer pattern.
sam_product: So feature tradeoff. For interactive UX we can't increase batch window globally. We need a smarter policy.
maya: Short-term mitigation: keep runtime v3.1.1 in prod-us-west; in next release revert dynamic-window change or make it configurable per route (low-latency routes get window=8ms). Long-term: adapt batch window based on observed QPS/latency SLAs.
jon_sre: I'll leave rollback in place and open an incident ticket summarizing steps and rollback timestamps for postmortem.
alex.g: Also let's add a temporary runtime-routing rule in the control plane to force low-latency customers to dedicated latency pool while we iterate.
kai_rt: Will submit PR to revert dynamic-window in the release branch and add config flag `batch.window_ms` per model-route.
lina_obs: Post-rollback verification: p95 back to ~130ms, p99 ~350ms, error rate unchanged. I'll keep monitoring for 2h and alert if anything drifts.
sam_product: Please update the support tickets with the rollback note and ETA for fix. I'll message affected customers.
maya: After action items: 
- kai: PR to revert/change batching (priority P0)
- lina: add dashboard for batch_size distribution and add alert if p99 queue_time > 500ms
- jon: incident doc + rollback timeline
- alex: coordinate customer comms
alex.g: Thanks all. Folks, quick heads-up for postmortem — include canary sampling policy (10% might be too small for this workload pattern) and consider adding synthetic traffic during canary to emulate burstiness.
kai_rt: Noted. I'll also add a canary smoke test that asserts p95/p99 thresholds with a bursty load pattern.
deploy-bot: Deployment note: v3.1.2 will be marked as deprecated in us-west.
alex.g: Marking thread resolved for now since rollback reduced customer impact. We'll keep monitoring. :thumbsup:
maya: Follow-up action: schedule a retro with product + runtime + obs this week.
jon_sre: Adding postmortem link once incident doc is ready.
lina_obs: Leaving monitoring alert on for 24h. If anything, ping me directly. :eyes:
kai_rt: Thanks everyone.
sam_product: Thanks — I'll update customers and close the high-priority tickets once 24h window is clean.
alex.g: Closing thread.
